subject: Week 29: crawling starts - babyproof at floor level now
bodyText:
This week
Crawling is underway for some - commando or quadrupedal - and a few infants pull to kneel or stand at furniture, though the CDC pull-to-stand checkpoint sits at 12 months, so no alarm if he stays planted. Babble is getting richer, with early imitation of your intonation, and lifting his arms to be picked up (a CDC 9-month checkpoint) turns communication deliberate. Stranger anxiety stays peaked; strong preference for you two is the design, not a bug.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Falling backward from sitting or forward onto his face while learning to crawl - bumps on soft surfaces are the cost of the curriculum.
- [monitor] No weight-bearing on his legs when held standing, or no banging two objects together as the 9-month checkpoint approaches - note it for the visit.
- [call within 24h] Persistent vomiting, or a new wheeze - RSV season is on.
- [call now] No wet diaper for more than 12 hours with lethargy, fever at or above 102F (rectal) with lethargy, or respiratory distress - call now; 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness.

Enrichment opportunities
- Run the babyproofing sweep at floor level this weekend: clear coins, batteries, magnets, and pet kibble from reach; put magnetic locks on medication and cleaning cabinets; add toilet locks; move toxic houseplants (pothos, philodendron, lily) up and out of range. AAP Childproofing Your Home: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/safety-prevention/at-home/Pages/Childproofing-Your-Home.aspx
- Practice supported standing daily - hold him at the hips at a low table for a few minutes; weight-bearing now feeds the pull-to-stand sequence later. AAP Movement: 8 to 12 Months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-8-to-12-Months.aspx
- Hand him a wooden spoon and a metal pot: banging two objects together is a CDC 9-month checkpoint, and the auditory payoff drives the repetition that builds it. CDC 9-month milestones: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/9-months.html
- Start baby sign at home if it appeals - five to 10 functional signs (milk, more, done), with signs back expected at 8-12 months. Calibration: the only longitudinal RCT found no language acceleration and a 17-study review supports no developmental claims; the plausible value is less frustration. It is free - skip the $200-350 paid class series. Hanen Centre on baby sign evidence: https://www.hanen.org/information-tips/does-baby-sign-make-a-difference

Upcoming
- Day 210 (early in the week of Dec 5, 2026): the live bilingual-exposure window effectively closes - if a bilingual nanny or immersion infant room is still on the table, commit this week; sub-threshold exposure buys familiarity, not phonology.
- Day 222-228 (week of Dec 19, 2026): holiday week - plan for disrupted naps and a re-run of the stranger-anxiety playbook with visiting family.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Responds to other people's emotional expressions
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Crying when a parent is sad, brightening when a parent laughs. Foundation of empathy.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/responds-to-others-emotions/complete

- Distinguishes emotions by tone of voice
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Reacts differently to a stern vs warm voice with the same words.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/distinguishes-emotion-tone/complete

- Finds a partially hidden object
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Beginning of object permanence — fully hidden objects come later.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/finds-partially-hidden-object/complete

- Struggles to reach objects that are out of reach
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Goal-directed behavior. Often precedes intentional rolling or scooting toward an object.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/struggles-for-out-of-reach/complete

- Begins to respond to the word 'no'
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Pauses briefly when the word is said. Compliance is a much later milestone.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/responds-to-no/complete
